shared_elements: low-relief carving on a flat stone surface
a horizontal band/register of repeated motifs (A: beaded/patterned bands on the garment; B: a band of repeated marks across the pillar head)
rounded disc-like element (A: earring/curl; B: small disc held by a figure)
justification: Both are shallow relief on a rectangular stone face with profile subjects and at least one horizontal band of repeated small motifs crossing the field, which is the most concrete correspondence. Otherwise they differ fundamentally: A is a single, large, anatomically detailed human head with finely stippled hair and beard filling the whole slab, while B is a stacked multi-register composition of schematic, flatly modelled animals on a T-shaped upright, executed with far coarser, more abstract cutting.
